also: write (a poem, a letter, a piece)

terms.gloss: compose, write (a book, a poem, a letter)
terms.comment: To put a written work together: books, speeches, letters, edicts, verses. Its first sense is “put together, arrange”, and it also means settle a quarrel and lay out the dead.
The plain everyday way to say it: versūs facere, poēma facere (Catull. 50.16, hoc, jūcunde, tibi poēma fēcī). For music, modōs facere (M-O s.v. compose (music), after Terence).
“Write” in general (see write); with carmen or versūs it is “write a poem”.

phrases.english: I made this poem for you, my dear friend

phrases.latin: sponte suā carmen numerōs veniēbat ad aptōs, et quod temptābam scrībere versus erat
phrases.english: of its own accord my song fell into the right rhythm, and whatever I tried to write came out as verse
